event_description: Statewide state of emergency for the record January 2000 snowstorm, declared January 25, 2000 (NPR that day; Hunt told CNN that morning he was prepared to call one).

State of emergency for the December 2002 ice storm, announced in the Governor's December 5, 2002 release "Gov. Easley Declares A State Of Emergency" (his December 9 release requests federal aid for the winter storm).
State of emergency for North Carolina ahead of Hurricane Isabel (Governor's release of September 16, 2003).
State of disaster and emergency for six eastern communities hit by the January 26-27, 2004 ice storm (Governor's release of June 4, 2004; Executive Order No. 59).
State of emergency for flooding from Tropical Depression Frances (Governor's release of September 7, 2004).
State of disaster for the Frances flooding, seeking an expedited federal declaration for 15 mountain counties (Governor's release of September 9, 2004).
State of emergency and disaster as the remnants of Hurricane Ivan struck the mountains (Governor's release of September 17, 2004).
Executive Order No. 88, state of emergency due to Hurricane Ophelia, declared September 11, 2005 (Governor's release of that day).
State of emergency to fight the wildfire in Hyde, Tyrrell and Washington counties (Governor's release of June 6, 2008).
Executive Order No. 144, state of emergency due to Tropical Storm Hanna and Hurricane Ike, declared Thursday, September 4, 2008 (WRAL that day).
State of emergency so heating fuel can be delivered during extreme winter cold (Governor's release of January 8, 2010).
Executive Order No. 62, state of emergency due to Hurricane Earl, declared at a Wednesday afternoon briefing, September 1, 2010 (CBS News that day).
State of emergency after the April 16, 2011 tornadoes (Governor's release of April 17, 2011; Executive Order No. 89 refers to the state of emergency caused by tornadoes).
State of emergency ahead of Hurricane Irene (Governor's release of August 25, 2011).
State of emergency for 33 eastern counties ahead of Hurricane Sandy (NCDPS release of October 26, 2012).
Executive Order No. 16, disaster declaration for Stanly County for the June 13, 2013 severe storms (Salisbury Post, July 10, 2013); the State Archives record is dated July 11.
Executive Order No. 17, disaster declaration for Orange County for the June 30, 2013 Chapel Hill flash flooding (WRAL reported it July 17); the State Archives record is dated July 16.
Executive Order No. 43, state of emergency ahead of the February 2014 winter storm of snow, sleet and ice (Salisbury Post, February 12, 2014); State Archives record dated February 11.
Executive Order No. 51, disaster declaration for the February 2014 winter storm for ten municipalities in southeastern North Carolina.
Executive Order No. 57, state of emergency for 26 counties due to Tropical Storm Arthur (FMCSA's copy, McCrory EO57.pdf, posted July 2, 2014).
Executive Order No. 66, state of emergency ahead of the February 16, 2015 winter storm of snow, sleet and freezing rain (WCCB that day).
Executive Order No. 97, state of emergency due to Tropical Storm Hermine (FMCSA's copy, McCrory EO 97 State of Emergency TS Hermine).
Executive Order No. 103, state of emergency for 11 northeastern counties for flooding from the remnants of Tropical Storm Julia (NCDPS release of September 22, 2016).
Executive Order No. 107, state of emergency for 66 counties ahead of Hurricane Matthew (NCDPS release of October 3, 2016).
Executive Order No. 115, state of emergency for 25 western counties for wildfires (NCDPS release of November 10, 2016).
